questions.q: What is the structural frame that carries a moving walk between its supports called?
o: Truss
Balustrade
Handrail
Pallet
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: As in an escalator, a steel truss spans between supports and carries the drive, tracks and pallets.

questions.q: What is the usual maximum slope of an inclined moving walk?
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook; EN 115
questions.n: Inclined moving walks are limited to about 12° so carts and people stay stable. Escalators may be 30°, or 35° for short rises.

questions.q: Why are moving walks often installed in pairs?
o: Because a single unit cannot run in reverse
So the two units can share one counterweight
So people can travel both ways and one can run while the other is serviced
Because codes forbid single units in public buildings
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Two units handle opposing flows. When one is down for maintenance, the other can keep running or be used as a walkway.

questions.q: Why might a moving walk be better than an elevator for a long horizontal corridor?
o: It carries more people per trip than a car
It needs no electrical power
It uses less floor area than an elevator
It moves people continuously, with no waiting for a car
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: People step on at any time, so there is no queue. Elevators are for vertical travel.

questions.q: A moving walk in a long airport concourse mainly solves which problem?
o: Long walking distances
Changes of floor level
Queuing at the gates
Baggage handling
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Moving walks cut walking time and effort over hundreds of metres, especially for travellers with bags.

questions.q: What does the comb assembly at a moving-walk landing do?
o: Drives the pallets around the loop
Guides feet and objects off the moving pallets onto the fixed floor
Guides the handrail where it turns
Keeps the pallet chain tight
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The comb teeth mesh with the pallet grooves at the landing. A switch stops the walk if something jams them.

questions.q: What is the basic difference between an escalator and a horizontal moving walk?
o: Escalators run on a belt; moving walks run on steps
Moving walks have no handrails
Escalators have stair steps that change level; moving walks have a flat surface
Escalators move faster than 2 m/s
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Escalator steps form stairs on the incline and flatten at the landings. Moving walks use flat pallets or a belt throughout.

questions.q: Why is maker's data needed before fixing a moving-walk opening and its supports?
o: All moving walks share one standard size
The data is needed only to choose finish colors
The structure does not interact with the equipment
Sizes, loads and support points differ from product to product
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Truss depth, pit size, support reactions and landing lengths vary with the model and length. Designing without them risks reworking the slab.

questions.q: What forms the moving surface of most moving walks?
o: Linked pallets or a continuous rubber belt
Stair steps with risers
Loose rollers set in the floor
Timber boards on a chain
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Pallet types are like flat escalator steps. Belt types run a rubber belt over rollers and are used for shorter walks.

questions.q: Which disciplines must coordinate on a moving-walk installation?
o: Architecture and interior design only
Architecture, structure, electrical and mechanical, accessibility and fire safety
Structural engineering only
Electrical engineering only
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The walk needs a pit and supports, power and controls, safe landings, a compliant alternative route and fire-safety coordination.

questions.q: How does an inclined moving walk differ from an escalator?
o: It has stair-shaped steps with risers
It always runs faster than an escalator
Its surface stays flat, so carts and trolleys can ride it
It is steeper than a standard escalator
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Supermarket and airport ramps use inclined walks so trolleys with locking wheels can ride. They are limited to about 12°.

questions.q: Which building type gains most from long horizontal moving walks?
o: Two-storey house
Small clinic
Neighborhood chapel
Airport terminal
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Airports and big transit stations have long level concourses where walking takes minutes.

questions.q: What is true of moving walks and accessibility?
o: A moving walk alone may not meet accessibility rules; a compliant alternative route may be needed
Every moving walk meets all accessibility rules
Moving walks are banned in public buildings
Only stairs may be provided beside them
questions.n: BP 344 requires an alternative pedestrian route near escalators and conveyors, clearly signed, since not everyone can ride them.

questions.q: What matters most when an inclined moving walk will carry people with luggage and carts?
o: The color of the pallets
The slope, the landing transitions and whether the carts suit the walk
The noise of the drive
The pattern of the side panels
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Steep slopes and abrupt transitions tip carts and bags. Carts need brakes or wheels that lock into the pallet grooves.

questions.q: What is the moving handrail of a moving walk for?
o: Driving the pallets along the track
Carrying the passengers' weight to the truss
A handhold that moves at about the same speed as the walk
Sealing the gap at the comb plate
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The handrail runs in step with the pallets so riders stay balanced. If it lags or stops, a monitor stops the walk.

questions.q: What should be checked at the entry and exit of a moving walk?
o: Extra lighting over the middle of the walk
A floor drain under the pallets
Wider pallets than at mid-run
Enough clear space for people to get on, get off and move away without crowding
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: People slow down as they step off. Without clear run-off space, they pile up at the exit and fall.

questions.q: What is a moving walk meant to do?
o: Carry people along a horizontal or gently sloped path
Lift people vertically between many floors
Replace every stair in a building
Carry freight in warehouses
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Moving walks (passenger conveyors) are for level or gently inclined travel, not for vertical transport.

questions.q: Why is an elevator better than a moving walk for a 15-storey building?
o: Moving walks are made for tall vertical travel
Elevators give direct vertical service to many floors
Elevators need no shafts or pits
Moving walks cannot carry people
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: A moving walk cannot change more than a small level difference. Only elevators serve many floors directly.
